learningObjective: Explain what a Grouped GEMM is and why it is preferred over per-expert independent GEMMs in sparse MoE serving.

canonicalClaims.claim: Grouped GEMM executes many independent GEMMs of varying shape as a single kernel launch, dispatching per-group tile schedules across SMs; this amortizes launch overhead and avoids SM under-utilization from small variable-size problems like MoE expert GEMMs.
conditions: Per-group problem sizes are known before launch.
SMs can pick tiles from any group per its schedule.
nonImplications: Does not eliminate token permutation cost.

misconceptions.claim: Grouped GEMM refers to reducing outputs across experts in one kernel.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Grouping is over independent GEMM problems, not over a reduction axis.

misconceptions.claim: Padded batched GEMM is always superior to grouped GEMM.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Padding wastes compute proportional to imbalance; grouped GEMM avoids that waste.

misconceptions.claim: Grouped GEMM reduces FLOPs via a Winograd-like transform.
misconceptions.whyWrong: No transform is involved; grouped GEMM is just a scheduling optimization.

implementationFacts: MegaBlocks and CUTLASS both provide grouped GEMM primitives for MoE.
In inference, grouped GEMM is applied to the up and down projections in the MoE MLP.
performanceScenarios: The win over per-expert launches grows with the number of experts and with imbalance.
The win over padded batched GEMM grows with imbalance in n_i.
